html:
In May 2024 riots broke out in Nouméa after the French parliament moved to open the frozen electoral roll of New Caledonia to more recent residents. Kanak groups saw it as a way to outvote them.

Barricades went up, businesses were burned, and more than a dozen people died. France declared a state of emergency, flew in police and soldiers, and later paused the reform.

The damage hit an economy already in trouble from the nickel crisis, and thousands lost their jobs. The unrest showed that the questions left open by the Nouméa Accord were still unresolved. See also Kanak people.
